record.question: When the sun is located in the shortest distance from the earth, it is called
record.explanation: Answer A: Perigee. Perigee is defensible under the source's Earth-centred wording: it asks when the Sun is closest to Earth. The US Naval Observatory's Astronomical Almanac glossary explicitly says perigee is sometimes used for the Sun's apparent orbit around Earth. In the usual heliocentric description, the same Earth–Sun closest approach is Earth's perihelion. None of the other printed terms denotes closest approach. Historical/source note: Earth-centred apparent solar-orbit terminology. In a heliocentric account say Earth at perihelion; the Sun does not physically orbit Earth. Reference: https://aa.usno.navy.mil/faq/asa_glossary; https://science.nasa.gov/learn/basics-of-space-flight/glossary/. Verified worked solution, unofficial. Historical facts are anchored to the original exam; no matching examiner key is asserted.
